question:
During a school athletics practice, a tracking device records an athlete's motion on a rectangular field. The athlete covers a total distance of $650\,\text{m}$ in $100\,\text{s}$ and has a displacement represented by $\vec{d}=300\hat{i}+400\hat{j}$ metres, where $\hat{i}$ points east and $\hat{j}$ points north. The athlete's mass is recorded as $50\,\text{kg}$. The students use these readings to distinguish scalar quantities from vector quantities and to analyse the athlete's resultant motion.

(a) Classify distance, time, mass and displacement as scalars or vectors.

(b) Calculate the magnitude of the displacement.

(c) Determine the direction of the displacement measured north of east.

(d) Calculate the athlete's average velocity vector and its magnitude.
explanation:
(a)Distance, time and mass possess magnitude only and are therefore scalar quantities. Displacement possesses both magnitude and direction and is therefore a vector quantity.

(b)The magnitude of the displacement is`|\vec{d}|=\sqrt{300^2+400^2}|\vec{d}|=\sqrt{250000}=500\,\text{m}`

(c)Let $\theta$ be the direction measured north of east. Then`\tan\theta=\frac{400}{300}=\frac{4}{3}`Therefore,\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\approx53.13^\circThe displacement is directed approximately $53.13^\circ$ north of east.

(d)Average velocity is displacement divided by time.`\vec{v}=\frac{\vec{d}}{100}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\,\text{m s}^{-1}`Its magnitude is`|\vec{v}|=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\,\text{m s}^{-1}`Thus, the average velocity is $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ with magnitude $5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

options.A:
(a) Distance and time are scalars; mass and displacement are vectors.
(b) $500\,\text{m}$
(c) $36.87^\circ$ north of east
(d) $\vec{v}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, $|\vec{v}|=5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$
options.B:
(a) Distance, time and mass are scalars; displacement is a vector.
(b) $700\,\text{m}$
(c) $53.13^\circ$ north of east
(d) $\vec{v}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, $|\vec{v}|=7\,\text{m s}^{-1}$
options.C:
(a) Distance, time and mass are scalars; displacement is a vector.
(b) $500\,\text{m}$
(c) $53.13^\circ$ north of east
(d) $\vec{v}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, $|\vec{v}|=5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$
options.D:
(a) Distance and displacement are vectors; time and mass are scalars.
(b) $500\,\text{m}$
(c) $36.87^\circ$ north of east
(d) $\vec{v}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, $|\vec{v}|=5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$
